review_notes:
I read all three proofs in the file (lines 1–73). I also read the statements of the lemmas they call: `spectralSecondFlux_primitive`, `spectralFirstFlux_primitive`, `spectralSecondFlux_hasDerivAt` and `spectralSecondClassicalFlux_eq` in the local project, plus Mathlib's `ae_of_mem_of_ae_of_mem_inter_Ioo` and `HasDerivAt.continuousOn`.

There is one supported finding. In two places the proofs rebuild `ContinuousOn` by hand from pointwise `HasDerivAt`, and Mathlib already has a named lemma for exactly that.

Other candidates I considered and rejected:
- Rewriting `rw [hx hxr]; exact (...).symm` as one `.trans` term.
- Replacing the closing `filter_upwards [hlocal] with x hx hxr; exact hx hxr.2` with `hlocal.mono`.
- Sharing the repeated `hl.trans hα.1`.

These are matters of taste or would not make the proofs clearer, so I did not report them. Some uncertainty remains: I could not run Lean, so the replacement is untested. In particular, I did not check that Lean infers the implicit derivative function `f'` from `hP`. Since `f'` is applied to the bound variable `x`, this is a standard higher-order pattern and should be inferred.

findings.problem: In both `spectralSecondClassicalFlux_ae` (line 43) and `spectralFirstClassicalFlux_ae` (line 67), the `ContinuousOn P (Ioo _ _)` argument to `spectralLocalFlux_classical_ae` is built by hand from `hP : ∀ x ∈ Ioo _ _, HasDerivAt P (_ x) x`. The anonymous function does this by chaining `continuousAt.continuousWithinAt`. That lambda is word for word the body of Mathlib's `HasDerivAt.continuousOn`.
findings.proposed_change: Replace `(fun x hx => (hP x hx).continuousAt.continuousWithinAt)` with `(HasDerivAt.continuousOn hP)` on both lines. For example, line 43 becomes `    (HasDerivAt.continuousOn hP) hflux`, and line 67 changes the same way.
findings.benefit: The lemma name states the mathematical point directly: a function with a derivative at every point of the interval is continuous there. The reader no longer has to work through a lambda and a two-step filter coercion chain. Nothing becomes more opaque, because it is an ordinary, well-named Mathlib lemma applied to the hypothesis that the lambda already uses. The same change would apply to the many identical lambdas elsewhere in the project, such as in SpectralForcedClassicalAE.lean and SpectralPencilFlux.lean.
